A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CarbonSense dataset and EcoPerceiver model. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered analyses.

before.justification: v1 reports original EcoPerceiver and XGBoost experiments across ten seeds, architectural ablations, ecosystem-specific training, and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, component ablations, and analysis of the dataset's temporal distribution.

M1.justification: The proposed EcoPerceiver retains its Fourier and spectral encodings, modality masking, windowed cross-attention, causal self-attention, and regression output. The additional transformer and ablated architectures are experimental comparators; the final model configuration remains unchanged.

E1.justification: The CarbonSense sites, ecosystems, and NEE prediction task remain unchanged. v2 adds explicit image-free training/inference and gapfilled-input evaluations in Appendix B.7.1, modestly extending input-condition coverage. The temporal histogram describes existing data.

E2.justification: v1 compares EcoPerceiver principally against XGBoost. v2 Appendix B.6 and Tables 8–9 add evaluated linear regression, random forest, and vanilla-transformer baselines across all 15 ecosystem types, substantially broadening the comparison.

E3.justification: The primary splits, training budgets, preprocessing threshold, and metrics remain unchanged. For ablations, v1 describes truncating plot axes, whereas v2 explicitly reports excluding the WAT test site. Added controls include gapfilled inputs and a six-layer, single-timestep transformer. These are reported evaluation changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's context-window, causal-masking, and observational-dropout tests, v2 examines Fourier encoding, satellite imagery, gap filling, and comparison with a vanilla transformer (B.7, Figure 11, Table 10). It also adds temporal dataset analysis. The ecosystem-specific experiment and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds pairwise NSE t-tests with nine degrees of freedom to Table 2 and numerical cross-ecosystem dispersion summaries to Table 10. The primary ten-seed practice remains unchanged; ablations still use one seed, now identified as 00. Their standard deviations describe ecosystem variation rather than uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 8–10 add substantial baseline and ablation results. For example, the newly evaluated transformer has WAT NSE −9.6845, compared with EcoPerceiver's −14.4010. All 60 original NSE/RMSE values in Table 2, the ecosystem-specific results, and the context-window plots are retained; the expansion does not establish improved same-setting EcoPerceiver performance.

T1.justification: The Fourier encoding equation, attention-complexity argument, and NSE definition are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and v2 adds no substantive theoretical development.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions: an ML-ready multimodal carbon-flux dataset, EcoPerceiver, and evidence that multimodal deep learning can improve prediction. The added experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as supporting imagery and in-model missing-data handling. It explicitly acknowledges that the transformer performance gap could reflect either WCA or access to temporal context, and explains WAT's exclusion from ablations. Existing geographic limitations and the rationale for causal masking remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the added transformer's six encoder layers, single-timestep inputs, shared tokenization, and linear readout, plus the new ablation configurations. Figure 8 newly specifies that pre-2000 observations lack MODIS data. Original hardware, optimization details, hyperparameters, and resource-access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Jung et al. (2011) and Vaswani et al. (2017), and a short history of regional and global flux modelling in Section 2. Papale and Valentini (2003), now discussed there, was already cited in v1. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 adds historical context and a model-comparison subsection, organizes ablations into architectural and context-window subsections, clarifies input-encoding language, and removes the checklist.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 2 with statistical-test columns, adds Tables 8–10 and the temporal-distribution Figure 8, and redraws the architectural ablation plots for seven variants. It also adopts the ICLR layout and relocates several displays. Existing performance boxplots, context-window plots, and qualitative traces are matched rather than counted as new.

improvement.justification: The added neural and tabular baselines and targeted component tests substantially address v1's narrow comparative validation and limited evidence for architectural choices (B.6–B.7). Statistical tests further improve assessment of the unchanged headline results. Single-seed ablations, WAT exclusion, and the acknowledged architecture-versus-context confound still limit conclusions, but the expanded evidence materially strengthens the paper.
